description: Accelerates the floating-point matrix multiplication kernel using a 2-element dot-product instruction.

instructions.name: Float Dot Product 2
instructions.semantics: This instruction computes a 2-element single-precision floating point dot product. The RED ABI expects `rs1` to be a pointer to a 5-word input block in memory, and `rs2` to be a pointer to a 5-word output block. The input block `in[0..4]` contains five 32-bit floating-point values: `in[0]` is the scalar accumulator `C`. `in[1]` and `in[2]` are elements from vector A. `in[3]` and `in[4]` are elements from vector B. The instruction computes `C = C + (A0 * B0) + (A1 * B1)` using standard round-to-nearest-even semantics, accumulating sequentially (`(C + A0*B0) + A1*B1`). To guarantee strictly constant-time hardware execution without an FPU, it explicitly flushes subnormal inputs and intermediate/output values to zero, canonizes NaNs, and silently discards all floating-point exceptions without modifying the FCSR. The computed single-precision float is written to `out[0]`. The remaining output words `out[1]` through `out[4]` are zero-padded. The architectural register `rd` is written with 0.

name: matrixmul_fdot
